# LinkedIn

77 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 3 standard (1 credit), 56 advanced (5), 8 premium (10), 10 custom (flat/metered) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

## GET /v1/linkedin/ad - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns one LinkedIn Ad Library ad as a canonical Post: `content.text` (the ad copy), `content.media_urls` and `thumbnail_url` (the creative), `author.display_name` and `avatar_url` (the advertiser), `published_at` (the campaign start date) and `engagement.views` (total impressions, when LinkedIn publishes them). Reaction, comment and share counts are not exposed on this surface and are null, and no targeting breakdown is returned. `author.username` currently repeats the advertiser NAME because the source sends no advertiser slug; join on the name, not on it.

**Use when** Use it after ads/search, passing an ad's Ad Library URL to read that single ad in full.
**Cost** cache 1800 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn ad · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/detail/1515437353`

**Contract**

- `post.ext.ad.payer` is who paid for the ad, often the media agency rather than the advertiser; `post.ext.ad.advertiser_profile_id` is the advertiser's LinkedIn company id.
- `post.ext.ad.format` and `format_label`, `headline`, `cta_texts`, `link_url`, `end_date`, `video_url` and `video_renditions` (url, content type, bitrate, label) describe the creative; `targeting` carries LinkedIn's EU targeting disclosure where it publishes one.

**Response** `Post` object at `data`, `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/Post.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+23 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name}; `post.content` {media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {views}; `post.flags` {deleted}; `post.ext.ad` {link_url, advertiser_profile_id, advertiser_profile_url, cta_texts, end_date, format, format_label, headline, payer} (+4 more). Never filled: `post.author.verified`, `post.content.duration_seconds`, `post.engagement.comments`, `post.engagement.likes`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.pinned`, `post.flags.spoiler`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/ad" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/detail/1515437353" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/ads/search - 5 credits (advanced)

Searches the LinkedIn Ad Library for ads by company, keyword, or filters. Returns matching ads with ad copy and sponsor info.

**Use when** you want to find what a competitor is running, then pass a result's ad URL to ad for the complete record.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** cursor (native `paginationToken`) · ≈24/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/24) x 5 credits · typical 6.8-9.1 s

**Query params**

- `company` (optional, string) - The company name to search for. 'Microsoft' for example · e.g. `microsoft`
- `keyword` (optional, string) - The keyword to search for
- `companyId` (optional, string) - The company id to search for
- `countries` (optional, string) - Comma separated list of countries. Example: US,CA,MX
- `startDate` (optional, string) - Start date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `endDate` (optional, string) - End date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `paginationToken` (optional, string) - Pagination token to paginate through results
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `company`, `keyword`, `companyId`.

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]` (inferred from a sample): {id string, description string, headline string, poster string, targeting object, image string, video null, preRollVideo null, organicVideo null, preRollAdvertiser null, carouselImages array, url string, adType string, creativeType string, advertiser string, advertiserLinkedinPage string, advertiserLogo string, cta string, sponsoredMessageSender null, sponsoredMessageSenderAvatar null, sponsoredMessageButtons array, destinationUrl null, landingPage null, adDuration string, startDate null} (+4 more).

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/ads/search" \
  --data-urlencode "company=microsoft" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/article - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns one Pulse article as a canonical Post: text, author, engagement, and publish time. Pass the article's `/pulse/` URL. Comments and reactions are separate calls.

**Use when** you have a /pulse/ URL. Comments and reactions are article/comments and article/reactions.

**Paging** none

| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

+16 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name, verified}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, saves, shares, views}; `post.ext` {published_at_precision}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post` {url string}; `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null} (+11 more).

```bash
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/article/comments - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns comments on a Pulse article as a canonical CommentList: commenter identity, text, and timestamp. Each comment also carries its LinkedIn link (`comment.url`), whether the commenter is a member or a page (`comment.ext.author_type`), the commenter's member urn (`comment.ext.author_urn`) and whether the thread has more replies than the row carries (`comment.ext.has_previous_replies`); each is null when the source does not give it, and `comment.ext.is_contribution` is null on this endpoint. Pass the article URL from `/v1/linkedin/article` or `/v1/linkedin/profile/articles`.

**Use when** Use it after article or profile/articles, passing the article URL.
**Cost** cache 300 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** page (native `page`) · ≈10/page (observed) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/10) x 5 credits · typical 2.3-2.3 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn Pulse article. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/2024-corporate-climate-pivot-bill-gates-u89mc/`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - 1-based page number. Defaults to 1.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `CommentList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ comment, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/CommentList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `comment.text` | Comment body. |
| `comment.id` | Platform-specific comment ID (always a string) |
| `comment.published_at` | Comment creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `comment.url` | Direct URL to the comment on the source platform |
| `comment.author.username` | Comment author username (null when tombstoned) |
| `comment.post_id` | ID of the post this comment belongs to |

+16 more (types in the full schema): `comment.author` {display_name}; `comment.engagement` {likes, replies}; `comment.ext` {author_headline, author_id, author_type, author_urn, has_previous_replies, is_contribution, is_edited, is_submitter, previous_replies_token, urn}; `comment.flags` {deleted, pinned}; `computed` {language}. Also in the sample: `comment` {parent_id null}; `comment.author` {avatar_url string, verified null} (+1 more). Page-level: `data.comment_recency`, `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/article/comments" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/2024-corporate-climate-pivot-bill-gates-u89mc/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/article/reactions - 5 credits (advanced)

**Use when** Use it after article, passing the same Pulse URL.
**Cost** cache 300 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** page (native `page`) · page size not measured · depth unknown · typical 2.0-2.1 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn Pulse article. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/2024-corporate-climate-pivot-bill-gates-u89mc/`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - 1-based page number. Defaults to 1.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |

+11 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, following, likes_count, posts_count, verified}; `author.ext` {account_type, business_hours, products, reaction_type, urn, public_identifier}. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

**Next** `linkedin/profile` (`url` ← `data.items[].author.url`) - Get LinkedIn user profile.


## GET /v1/linkedin/company - 5-8 credits (request-shaped)

Returns public information about a LinkedIn company page. Canonical fields carry the identity and reach: `author.id` (the numeric company_id the other `/company/*` endpoints take), `username`, `display_name`, `bio` (the company description), `avatar_url` (logo), `followers`, `location` (flattened HQ), and `verified`. The complete **About tab** rides in `author.ext`: `website`, `public_phone` (the phone number the page lists), `employee_count` and `employee_count_range`, `founded_year`, `specialities[]`, `industries[]`, `headquarters` (structured `{country, city, geographic_area, line1, line2, postal_code}`), `locations[]` (every office LinkedIn lists, with lat/long), `hashtags[]`, `cover_url`, and `page_active`. Fields a page has not filled in come back null rather than omitted, so `founded_year` is null on a company that never set a founding date and `public_phone` is null on a page that lists no phone. The record also includes, where LinkedIn shows them, `company_type` (LinkedIn's "Type", for example "Public Company" or "Privately Held") with its stable code `company_type_code` (`PUBLIC_COMPANY`), the `tagline` (the page's one-line slogan), the website's `domain`, `page_type` (`company`, `school` or `showcase`), the full founding date `founded_on` (`{year, month, day}`), the `is_claimable`, `is_archived` and `is_auto_generated` page flags, `verification_updated_at` (when LinkedIn last changed the page's verification record), each office's `label` and `is_headquarters` in `locations[]` (and the headquarters' `label`), and, when the answering source carries them, `call_to_action_url`, `industry_id`, `industry_hierarchy`, `is_premium` (a paid Premium page), `public_phone_extension`, `crunchbase_url`, `open_job_count` and `products`. Add `include=about` to make sure of the company type and tagline: it looks them up only when the plain answer came back without the company type, and when the plain answer already carries the company type, it runs no lookup and costs nothing extra. When a backup source answers, `verified` and `page_active` can be null and `data._warnings` says which fields it could not fill. `funding` is mapped too, but LinkedIn returned an empty funding block for every company measured on 11/08/2026, so do not depend on it.

**Use when** you want to look up a company by its page URL, and to get the numeric company_id that the other company endpoints need.
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits for the company page. include=about holds 3 more and keeps them only when it fills the company type or tagline the plain call lacked, refunding them otherwise, so a call with include=about is at most 8 credits; when the plain answer already carries the company type, no lookup runs and it settles at 5. Company lookups are cached.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn company page · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/company/microsoft/`
- `include` (optional, enum: about) - Set to `about` (one token only) to add the page's company type (`author.ext.company_type`, for example "Public Company") and tagline (`author.ext.tagline`) when the plain call returned without them. 3 extra credits, kept only when one of the two comes back; a page that sets neither is refunded, and so is a call whose plain answer already carries the company type, because no lookup runs. Usually adds 1 to 4 seconds when a lookup runs, and up to 36 seconds when the first source cannot answer and the backup sources are slow; read `data.hydration` for the credits held and kept and the time.

**Response** `Author` object at `data`, `{ author, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/Author.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `author.id` | 100% | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | 100% | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.username` | 100% | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | 100% | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | 100% | Display name or full name |

+45 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, verified, location}; `author.ext` {employee_count, industries, locations, page_active, specialities, website, business_hours, call_to_action_url, company_type, company_type_code, cover_url, crunchbase_url, domain}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach} (+26 more). Page-level: `data.hydration`.

**Next** `linkedin/company/posts` (`company_id` ← `data.author.id`) - The company page's latest posts. · `linkedin/company/jobs` (`company_id` ← `data.author.id`) - The company's open jobs. · `linkedin/company/also-viewed` (`company_id` ← `data.author.id`) - List company pages people also viewed. · `linkedin/company/affiliated-pages` (`company_id` ← `data.author.id`) - List a company's affiliated/showcase pages.

```bash

  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/company/microsoft/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/company/people - 10-50 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a paginated list of members who work at a company, with handle, headline, location, and member URN. Get the company_id from /v1/linkedin/company. Each page is 10 members. On a plain call `author.followers` is LinkedIn's rounded display bucket, and only on the rows that show one (flagged `author.ext.followers_approximate: true`), and `author.following` is null on every row. When the primary source is momentarily rate-limited on page 1, a second source answers that page with current members of the same company in a different order and with exact follower counts (`author.ext.followers_approximate: false`), and `data._warnings` says so; page 2 onwards always comes from the primary, so a member can repeat or be missed across that boundary. Send `include=profile` and every row is joined, in the same call, to the member's profile lookup (`/v1/linkedin/profile`): `author.followers` becomes the exact follower count and `author.ext.followers_approximate` reads false on every row the lookup filled, whether the row arrived with LinkedIn's rounded bucket or with no count at all, `author.following` is filled with the member's connection count (on LinkedIn a member's `following` is the number of connections), and the location, the joined date (`author.joined_at`), and the country, website, cover image and profile flags on `author.ext` land where the row lacks them. Cost: 10 credits for the list; include=profile holds 4 credits per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup, so a call costs at most 50; rows already in cache are free and unfilled rows are refunded. Pass `limit` (1 to 10) to join only the top rows: `limit=3&include=profile` costs at most 22. Time: the lookups run in parallel, about 1 second for 10 rows, up to 3 on a slow second, and never more than 8 seconds. The response carries a `hydration` block itemising rows, lookups, cache hits, credits and milliseconds.

**Use when** you already have a company_id and want its staff; use search/people to filter across all of LinkedIn instead.
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 10 credits for the list. include=profile holds 4 credits per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup: at most 50 for the 10-row page, or 10 + 4 x limit when you pass `limit`. Rows served from cache are free, unfilled rows are refunded, and a repeat of a fully joined page within the list's cache window costs 0. The list is cached for 15 minutes and each profile lookup for 15 minutes. With `max_pages`, `max_items` or `max_credits`, each page walked is billed at this price (a cached page is free), and `max_credits` caps the total.
**Paging** page (native `page`) · default page size not measured; set with `limit` · depth unknown · typical 13-29 s

**Query params**

- `company_id` (required) - LinkedIn numeric company ID (from /v1/linkedin/company). · e.g. `1035`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - Page number for pagination (default 1).
- `include` (optional, enum: profile) - Set to `profile` (one token only) to join every row to the member's profile lookup in this one call: `author.followers` becomes the exact count and `author.ext.followers_approximate` reads false on every row the lookup filled, `author.following` is filled with the member's connection count, and the location, joined date, country, website, cover image and profile flags land where the row lacks them. Holds 4 credits per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup; rows already in cache and rows that could not be filled are refunded, so a call costs at most 50 (10 + 4 per row) and the usual bill is lower. Adds about 1 second for 10 rows, up to 3 on a slow second and never more than 8, and nothing when the members are already cached; read `data.hydration` for the rows, the credits held and kept, and the time.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-10) - Take the top N rows of this page (1 to 10). With `include=profile` it caps both the rows joined and the extra credits: `limit=3&include=profile` costs at most 22. The page cursor still advances past the full page of 10, so the rows past your limit are skipped, not carried to the next page. Without `include=profile` the call stays 10 credits.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |

+22 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, following, joined_at, likes_count, location, posts_count, verified}; `author.ext` {business_hours, country, cover_url, followers_approximate, is_creator, is_hiring, is_influencer, is_open_to_work, is_premium, is_top_voice, joined_at_precision, member_id} (+3 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.hydration`, `data.walk`.

```bash
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/company/posts - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns recent posts from a LinkedIn company page as the same PostList shape as `/v1/linkedin/profile/posts`: text, reaction/comment/share counts, the company slug on `post.author.username`, and `content.media_urls` / `thumbnail_url` when the row is an image, a video or an article share. Video duration is `content.duration_seconds`. The company's follower count rides on `post.ext.author_followers`. When a backup source serves the page, `data.total` is null because that source states no total, `post.ext.share_urn` can be missing on reposted posts, and `data._warnings` says so. A `next_cursor` it returns continues through the same source. Any page can repeat a post you already received, so de-duplicate on `post.id`; walk the pages in one sitting, because a late cursor overlaps more. A cursor the source refuses answers a free 400; start again from the first page by sending the same request without `cursor`. Where LinkedIn shows them, each post also carries the accounts it mentions and its linked text ranges (`post.ext.mentioned_accounts`, `post.ext.text_entities`, `post.ext.outbound_links`), whether it was edited or has comments turned off (`post.ext.is_edited`, `post.ext.comments_disabled`), its kind (`post.ext.type`, `post.ext.media_type`), a document, poll, job, event, celebration card or newsletter edition (`post.ext.document`, `post.ext.poll`, `post.ext.job`, `post.ext.event`, `post.ext.celebration`, `post.ext.newsletter`), the post it quotes (`post.ext.quoted_post`), who reposted it and when (`post.ext.reposted_by`, `post.ext.reposted_at`), the button on the author's profile (`post.ext.author_website`, `post.ext.author_website_label`) and a video's aspect ratio (`post.ext.aspect_ratio`); each is null when the post has none or it could not be read for that post. On this endpoint only one of our sources reads those post fields, so they are null on pages the main source serves and filled when that source serves the page: the mentions and text ranges, the edited and comments flags, the kind of post, the job, event, celebration, newsletter, quoted post, reposter and the author's profile button.

**Use when** you want it for what a brand publishes; profile/posts covers an individual member and group/posts covers a group feed.
**Cost** cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** page (native `page`) · ≈50/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/50) x 5 credits · typical 3.6-17 s

**Query params**

- `company_id` (required) - LinkedIn numeric company ID (from /v1/linkedin/company). · e.g. `1035`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - Page number for pagination (default 1).
- `sort_by` (optional, enum: top | recent) - Post ordering: 'top' or 'recent'.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off the page, and the page that reaches one ends the walk: `next_cursor` is not returned and `pagination.stopped_at` is `since`. Sending it sets the newest-first sort shown in this endpoint's sort parameter (any other sort value is a free 400). The page still costs what a page costs, so you pay for the pages you walk and no more. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Constraints**

- `since` requires `sort_by=recent` (auto-injected when `sort_by` is absent; a different value is a free 400).

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ post, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | 100% | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | 100% | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | 100% | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | 100% | Author username |
| `post.author.display_name` | 100% | Author display name |
| `post.engagement.comments` | 100% | Comment count. |

+31 more (types in the full schema): `post.engagement` {likes, shares}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.ext` {aspect_ratio, author_website, author_website_label, celebration, comments_disabled, document, event, is_edited, job, media_type, mentioned_accounts, newsletter} (+12 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash

  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/post - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns detailed information about a specific LinkedIn post including the post text, like count, comment count, share count, author info, media attachments, and publish timestamp.

**Which post URL to send.** A LinkedIn post can be addressed by three different ids, and this endpoint resolves the ACTIVITY one: `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>`, or the share-button form `https://www.linkedin.com/posts/<slug>-activity-<id>-<code>`. A `urn:li:share:` or `urn:li:ugcPost:` URL is a different id for the same post and cannot be resolved here, so it is rejected with a 400 before any credits are charged. The reliable way to get a URL that works is to read `post.url` off any endpoint that lists posts (/v1/linkedin/profile/posts, /v1/linkedin/company/posts, /v1/linkedin/search/posts and the rest): that field is always the activity form. Do not rebuild the URL from `post.id`, which on some endpoints is the share or ugcPost id rather than the activity id.

**Use when** you have a post URL and want the post itself, not its comments, reactions, or reposts.
**Cost** cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn post. It has to carry the post's ACTIVITY id, either `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>` or `https://www.linkedin.com/posts/<slug>-activity-<id>-<code>`. A `urn:li:share:` or `urn:li:ugcPost:` URL names a different id for the same post and is rejected with a 400 before any credits are charged, because it cannot be resolved to the post. Every endpoint that lists posts publishes the activity form as `post.url`, so copy that field rather than rebuilding the URL from `post.id`, which is not always the activity id. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7501466755261820928`

**Response** `Post` object at `data`, `{ post, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/Post.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | 100% | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | 100% | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | 100% | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | 100% | Author username |
| `post.author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to author profile picture |
| `post.author.display_name` | 100% | Author display name |

+11 more (types in the full schema): `post.engagement` {comments, likes, shares}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.flags` {deleted}; `post.content` {duration_seconds}; `post.ext` {published_at_precision}. Also in the sample: `post` {url string}; `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null, pinned null}; `post.ext` {author_id string, post_type string}; `post.ext.reaction_counts[]` {count number, type string} (+6 more). Never filled: `post.author.verified`, `post.content.media_urls`, `post.content.thumbnail_url`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.views`.

## GET /v1/linkedin/post/comments - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns a paginated list of comments on a LinkedIn post, with commenter identity, text, reaction breakdown, pin/edit flags, and reply counts. LinkedIn shows the newest reply of each thread under its comment, and so does this endpoint: it is in `comment.replies`, with its own author, text and time. `engagement.replies` is the thread's full count. When a thread has older replies than the one shown, the comment also carries `ext.previous_replies_token`; pass it as `cursor` to /v1/linkedin/post/comments/replies to read the rest, or call that endpoint without `cursor` for the whole thread. A one-reply thread has no token because its only reply is already in `comment.replies`. `ext.is_submitter` is true when the commenter wrote the post (LinkedIn's Author badge). Each comment also carries its own link on `comment.url` (a reply in `comment.replies` carries one where LinkedIn sends the reply's own id), the commenter's kind (`ext.author_type`, `user` or `company`) and, where LinkedIn shows them, the commenter's member URN (`ext.author_urn`), whether the comment is a contribution to a collaborative article (`ext.is_contribution`) and whether the thread has more replies than `comment.replies` holds (`ext.has_previous_replies`); each is null when the source that answered does not send it. A reply's `id` is LinkedIn's comment id when LinkedIn sends one; otherwise it is a stable id built from the parent comment's id (`<parent id>:<8 hex>`). When the main sources cannot answer, a backup source answers the same comments: there `comment.replies` holds every reply LinkedIn shows inline (not only the newest) with LinkedIn's own ids, links and like counts, a company page that commented carries its logo as `author.avatar_url` and its universal name as `author.username`, and each comment's `ext.reaction_counts` and `ext.previous_replies_token` are null, with `engagement.likes` still the total; `data._warnings` says so. If that source's relevance order comes back empty on page 1 of a post that has comments, it lists them newest first and `data._warnings` says that too. A repost keeps its comments on the original post, and some posts file them under their own post id, which differs from the id in the URL. LinkedIn's newest-first order (`sort_order=recent`, which `since` and its aliases set) comes back empty on such a URL, so that order is read from the post the comments are filed under, on every page, and `data._warnings` says which (a repost, or the post's own id). On any other post whose newest-first order comes back empty while it has comments, they are read in relevance order and listed newest first by date when they fit on one page, otherwise from the backup source's own newest-first order, and `data._warnings` says which. A post with no comments returns an empty page for free, and that empty answer is cached for 1 hour; send `Cache-Control: no-cache` to read it again sooner.

**Use when** you want it for the top-level comments on a post, then pass a comment's id to post/comments/replies to open one thread.
**Cost** cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** page (native `page`) · ≈3/page (observed) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/3) x 5 credits · typical 1.8-14 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn post. It has to carry the post's ACTIVITY id, either `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>` or `https://www.linkedin.com/posts/<slug>-activity-<id>-<code>`. A `urn:li:share:` or `urn:li:ugcPost:` URL names a different id for the same post and is rejected with a 400 before any credits are charged, because it cannot be resolved to the post. Every endpoint that lists posts publishes the activity form as `post.url`, so copy that field rather than rebuilding the URL from `post.id`, which is not always the activity id. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7244804629786419202`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - Page number for pagination (default 1).
- `post_type` (optional, enum: activity | ugc) - Upstream post type: 'activity' (default) or 'ugc'.
- `sort_order` (optional, enum: recent | relevance) - Comment ordering: 'relevance' or 'recent'.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off the page, and the page that reaches one ends the walk: `next_cursor` is not returned and `pagination.stopped_at` is `since`. Sending it sets the newest-first sort shown in this endpoint's sort parameter (any other sort value is a free 400). The page still costs what a page costs, so you pay for the pages you walk and no more. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Constraints**

- `since` requires `sort_order=recent` (auto-injected when `sort_order` is absent; a different value is a free 400).

**Response** `CommentList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ comment, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/CommentList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `comment.id` | Platform-specific comment ID (always a string) |
| `comment.text` | Comment body. |
| `comment.published_at` | Comment creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `comment.url` | Direct URL to the comment on the source platform |
| `comment.author.username` | Comment author username (null when tombstoned) |
| `comment.post_id` | ID of the post this comment belongs to |

+14 more (types in the full schema): `comment.author` {display_name}; `comment.engagement` {likes, replies}; `comment.ext` {author_headline, author_id, author_type, has_previous_replies, is_edited, is_submitter, previous_replies_token, urn}; `comment.flags` {deleted, pinned}; `computed` {language}. Also in the sample: `comment` {parent_id null}; `comment.author` {avatar_url null, verified null}; `comment.ext` {reaction_counts array}. ## GET /v1/linkedin/post/comments/replies - 5 credits (advanced)

Lists the replies under one LinkedIn comment, oldest first, each with its author, text, time, reaction breakdown and `ext.is_submitter` (true when the reply is by the post's author). Called without `cursor` it returns the whole thread. Called with the parent's `ext.previous_replies_token` as `cursor` it returns only the replies older than the newest one, which /v1/linkedin/post/comments already carries in `comment.replies`, so the two calls together are the thread with no overlap. Pass the parent comment's `comment.id`, or its `comment.ext.urn`, as `comment_id`; the urn is the faster route on posts published as images, video or documents. A thread read without `cursor` takes about 20 seconds, and up to about 30 on the first comment of such a post when only the bare id is passed.

**Use when** Use it after post/comments: pass that comment's comment_id together with the post url to expand a single thread.
**Cost** cache 300 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** cursor · page size not measured · depth unknown · typical 27-31 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn post. It has to carry the post's ACTIVITY id, either `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>` or `https://www.linkedin.com/posts/<slug>-activity-<id>-<code>`. A `urn:li:share:` or `urn:li:ugcPost:` URL names a different id for the same post and is rejected with a 400 before any credits are charged, because it cannot be resolved to the post. Every endpoint that lists posts publishes the activity form as `post.url`, so copy that field rather than rebuilding the URL from `post.id`, which is not always the activity id. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7501466755261820928`
- `comment_id` (required) - The parent comment's `comment.id` from /v1/linkedin/post/comments, or its `comment.ext.urn` (urn:li:comment:(ugcPost:<post>,<comment>)). · e.g. `7501480403283886080`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - LinkedIn cursor.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `CommentList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ comment, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/CommentList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `comment.text` | Comment body. |
| `comment.id` | Platform-specific comment ID (always a string) |
| `comment.published_at` | Comment creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `comment.url` | Direct URL to the comment on the source platform |
| `comment.author.username` | Comment author username (null when tombstoned) |
| `comment.post_id` | ID of the post this comment belongs to |

## GET /v1/linkedin/post/reactions - 10-50 credits (request-shaped)

Lists the members who reacted to a LinkedIn post as a canonical AuthorList: name, headline, profile URL, avatar and member URN (`author.ext.urn`), with the reaction they left on `author.ext.reaction_type` (filter it with `type`). Each page is 10 reactors; page through with `page`. On a plain call a reactor row carries no follower count, connection count or location: `author.followers` and `author.following` are null on every row. `author.username` carries the member's profile slug, and `author.url` their profile link (`https://www.linkedin.com/in/<slug>`), where LinkedIn exposes the slug: on the first page of an unfiltered call (`type` absent or `all`) it is read for each member, unless that read is slow or unavailable. Elsewhere both carry the member's URN form, as LinkedIn's reactor list links it. `author.ext.public_identifier` carries the slug too (null where it is not exposed), and `author.ext.account_type` says whether the reactor is a member (`user`) or a page (`company`). When a backup source answers an unfiltered call, a company page that reacted is listed too, with its page URL and its universal name as `author.username`. Send `include=profile` and every row is joined, in the same call, to the member's profile lookup (`/v1/linkedin/profile`): `author.followers` becomes the exact follower count and `author.ext.followers_approximate` reads false on every row the lookup filled, whether the row arrived with LinkedIn's rounded bucket or with no count at all, `author.following` is filled with the member's connection count (on LinkedIn a member's `following` is the number of connections), and the location, the joined date (`author.joined_at`), and the country, website, cover image and profile flags on `author.ext` land where the row lacks them. Cost: 10 credits for the list; include=profile holds 4 credits per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup, so a call costs at most 50; rows already in cache are free and unfilled rows are refunded. Pass `limit` (1 to 10) to join only the top rows: `limit=3&include=profile` costs at most 22. Time: the lookups run in parallel, about 1 second for 10 rows, up to 3 on a slow second, and never more than 8 seconds. The response carries a `hydration` block itemising rows, lookups, cache hits, credits and milliseconds.

**Use when** you want to see who liked or praised a post, optionally filtered by type; post/comments covers the people who wrote a comment.
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 300 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 10 credits for the list. include=profile holds 4 credits per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup: at most 50 for the 10-row page, or 10 + 4 x limit when you pass `limit`. Rows served from cache are free, unfilled rows are refunded, and a repeat of a fully joined page within the list's cache window costs 0. The list is cached for 5 minutes and each profile lookup for 15 minutes. With `max_pages`, `max_items` or `max_credits`, each page walked is billed at this price (a cached page is free), and `max_credits` caps the total.
**Paging** page (native `page`) · default page size not measured; set with `limit` · depth unknown · typical 3.2-5.0 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn post. It has to carry the post's ACTIVITY id, either `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>` or `https://www.linkedin.com/posts/<slug>-activity-<id>-<code>`. A `urn:li:share:` or `urn:li:ugcPost:` URL names a different id for the same post and is rejected with a 400 before any credits are charged, because it cannot be resolved to the post. Every endpoint that lists posts publishes the activity form as `post.url`, so copy that field rather than rebuilding the URL from `post.id`, which is not always the activity id. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7501466755261820928`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - 1-based page number. Defaults to 1.
- `type` (optional, enum: all | like | praise | empathy | appreciation | interest) - Filter by kind. See the allowed values.
- `include` (optional, enum: profile) - Set to `profile` (one token only) to join every row to the member's profile lookup in this one call: `author.followers` becomes the exact count and `author.ext.followers_approximate` reads false on every row the lookup filled, `author.following` is filled with the member's connection count, and the location, joined date, country, website, cover image and profile flags land where the row lacks them. Holds 4 credits per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup; rows already in cache and rows that could not be filled are refunded, so a call costs at most 50 (10 + 4 per row) and the usual bill is lower. Adds about 1 second for 10 rows, up to 3 on a slow second and never more than 8, and nothing when the members are already cached; read `data.hydration` for the rows, the credits held and kept, and the time.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-10) - Take the top N rows of this page (1 to 10). With `include=profile` it caps both the rows joined and the extra credits: `limit=3&include=profile` costs at most 22. The page cursor still advances past the full page of 10, so the rows past your limit are skipped, not carried to the next page. Without `include=profile` the call stays 10 credits.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |

+21 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, following, joined_at, location}; `author.ext` {account_type, business_hours, country, cover_url, is_creator, is_hiring, is_influencer, is_open_to_work, is_premium, is_top_voice, joined_at_precision, member_id, products, reaction_type, urn} (+2 more). Never filled: `author.likes_count`, `author.posts_count`, `author.verified`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.hydration`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/post/reactions" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7501466755261820928" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/post/reposts - 5 credits (advanced)

Lists the members and companies that reshared a LinkedIn post. Each row is one reshare: `post.author` is who reshared it, `post.id` and `post.url` identify the reshare itself, and `post.ext.is_repost_quote` says whether commentary was added. Two leaves come from the ORIGINAL post, because LinkedIn shows them that way on a reshare: `post.engagement` and `post.ext.reaction_counts` are the original post's totals, not the reshare's. `content.text` and `published_at` are not exposed on this surface and are null. Pagination is by `cursor`; the provider can re-serve the first page on page 2 for a post with few reshares.

**Use when** you want to see who amplified a post; post/reactions lists who reacted and post/comments lists who replied.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Paging** cursor · ≈10/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/10) x 5 credits · typical 10-17 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn post. It has to carry the post's ACTIVITY id, either `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>` or `https://www.linkedin.com/posts/<slug>-activity-<id>-<code>`. A `urn:li:share:` or `urn:li:ugcPost:` URL names a different id for the same post and is rejected with a 400 before any credits are charged, because it cannot be resolved to the post. Every endpoint that lists posts publishes the activity form as `post.url`, so copy that field rather than rebuilding the URL from `post.id`, which is not always the activity id. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7501466755261820928`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - LinkedIn cursor.
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - 1-based page number. Defaults to 1.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

+11 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {display_name}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, shares}; `post.ext` {is_repost_quote, published_at_precision, reaction_type}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post` {url string}; `post.content` {media_urls null, thumbnail_url null, duration_seconds null}; `post.author` {avatar_url string, verified null}; `post.engagement` {views null, saves null} (+8 more). Never filled: `post.ext.aspect_ratio`, `post.ext.author_website`, `post.ext.author_website_label`, `post.ext.celebration`, `post.ext.comments_disabled`, `post.ext.document`, `post.ext.event`, `post.ext.is_edited`, `post.ext.job`, `post.ext.media_type`, `post.ext.mentioned_accounts`, `post.ext.newsletter` (+8 more). ## GET /v1/linkedin/post/transcript - 10 credits (premium)

Fetches the transcript from a LinkedIn post video when LinkedIn exposes one publicly. A post with no caption track, or with no video at all, answers `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` with `details.reason: "no_captions"` and a message saying retrying will return the same result, so you can tell it apart from a transient failure and stop. Credits are only deducted when a transcript is actually returned.

**Reposts.** LinkedIn does not show a repost's content to logged-out viewers, so a repost URL is read from the original post it shares: the response carries a `_warnings` note naming the original post's URL (in `data._warnings`, or in `error.details._warnings` when the original has no transcript), and it costs the same as any other transcript request. A post that cannot be read logged-out and cannot be resolved to an original answers `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` with `details.reason: "post_not_public"`, at no charge.

**Use when** you want to read or search what was said in a LinkedIn video; you are only charged when a transcript actually comes back.
**Cost** cache 2592000 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn post to transcribe. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/posts/gemini-35-flash-is-a-step-forward-for-google-ugcPost-7465082215316525056-MHBd/`

**Response** `Transcript` object at `data`, `{ url, transcript, transcriptNotAvailable }` (inferred from a sample): {url string, transcript string, transcriptNotAvailable boolean}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/post/transcript" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/posts/gemini-35-flash-is-a-step-forward-for-google-ugcPost-7465082215316525056-MHBd/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns a LinkedIn member's public profile as a canonical Author: `display_name`, `username` (the vanity slug), `bio` (the headline), `location`, `avatar_url`, `url`, exact `followers` and `following` (connections), and `joined_at` (the account creation date). `author.ext` carries the member `urn` (the join key for every `/v1/linkedin/profile/*` sub-resource), `member_id`, `website`, `country`, the cover image, and the status flags (`is_premium`, `is_top_voice`, `is_creator`, `is_influencer`, `is_open_to_work`, `is_hiring`). The record also includes, where LinkedIn shows them, the About text (`author.ext.about`), the current position and school (`current_position`, `current_school`), the industry (`industry_id` is the stable key and the wording of the `industry` label can vary), the verification badge and its list (`author.verified`, `author.ext.verifications`), the first and last name, pronoun, locales, profile links (`bio_links`), hashtags, location id (`geo_id`) and volunteer causes. Experience, education and skills are separate sub-resources: use `/v1/linkedin/profile/experiences`, `/educations` and `/skills` (5 credits each). When the primary source is momentarily rate-limited, a second source answers with the same fields; on those answers `joined_at` is the first day of the month the member joined, because that source gives the month and year only. `author.ext.joined_at_precision` says which: `month` on such an answer, null when `joined_at` is the exact day.

**Use when** Use it as the starting point for any person lookup, then call the profile sub-endpoints for their experiences, skills, or posts. **Not for** a member's full background in one call (linkedin/profile/all), their posts (linkedin/profile/posts) or a company page (linkedin/company).
**Cost** cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile page · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/`

**Response** `Author` object at `data`, `{ author, computed }` (fill from 1 call) ([full schema](schemas/Author.md))

| Field | Fill | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `author.url` | 100% | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.id` | 100% | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.username` | 100% | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | 100% | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | 100% | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | 100% | Display name or full name |

+50 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, following, verified, location}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach}; `author.ext` {about, about_localized, bio_links, business_hours, cover_url, current_position, current_school, first_name, geo_id, hashtags, headline_localized, industry} (+31 more).

**Next** `linkedin/profile/posts` (`url` ← `data.author.url`) - The person's latest posts. · `linkedin/profile/complete` (`url` ← `data.author.url`) - The person's full profile in one call. · `linkedin/profile/articles` (`url` ← `data.author.url`) - List Pulse articles a LinkedIn member published. · `linkedin/profile/interests/companies` (`url` ← `data.author.url`) - List companies a member follows.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/about - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns LinkedIn's account-freshness panel for a member: `joined` (the month the account was created, as a label such as "May 2013"), and how recently the contact information and profile photo were updated. `is_verified` and `verification` (LinkedIn's identity verification details) appear only when LinkedIn's verification panel can be read for that member; otherwise the response carries no verification keys. **This is not the member's About/summary section**: despite the resource name, no free-text profile summary is returned. The closest public text LinkedIn publishes for a member is the headline, on `author.bio` from `/v1/linkedin/profile`. For a company's About tab, use `/v1/linkedin/company` (`author.ext`). The join date itself is already on `/v1/linkedin/profile` as `author.joined_at` (an exact date).

**Use when** you want to judge how current a profile is. Verification is included only for members whose verification panel can be read. Values come back as relative text, not exact dates.
**Cost** cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile, company, or post. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/`
- `urn` (optional, string) - The member's opaque LinkedIn URN, as returned in `author.ext.urn` by /v1/linkedin/profile. Optional, and a pure optimisation: pass it ALONGSIDE `url` (which stays required) and this call skips the internal handle lookup, so it answers faster and consumes half the upstream rate-limit budget. Verified on the deployed API 05/09/2026. To address a member by URN alone, send the URN-form profile URL as `url`, for example https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAA8BYqEBCGLg_vT_ca6mMEqkpp9nVffJ3hc: it resolves to the same member as the public address (verified 20/10/2026 on profile/posts and profile/comments) and holds only ASCII, which helps when the public address carries an emoji or other symbol.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data`, `{ joined, contact_information, profile_photo }` (inferred from a sample): {joined string, contact_information string, profile_photo string}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/about" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/all - 5-50 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a LinkedIn member's ENTIRE public profile in a single call, every section LinkedIn publishes. This is the endpoint for a one-call profile audit, and it replaces stacking `/profile`, `/profile/complete`, `/profile/stats`, the five `/profile/interests/*` endpoints and `/profile/similar`. `author` is the same Author object `/v1/linkedin/profile` returns, with `followers` and `following` filled, plus `verified`, `joined_at`, `ext.website`, `ext.is_influencer`, `ext.is_open_to_work`, `ext.is_hiring`, `ext.is_memorialized` and `ext.cover_url`; `verified` is null on every other LinkedIn endpoint and real here. `background` holds `summary` (the About text), `experiences`, `educations`, `skills`, `recommendations` (received), `current_position`, `top_education`, `certifications`, `honors`, `languages`, `projects`, `publications`, `volunteering`, `courses`, `patents`, `organizations`, `causes`, `top_skills`, `featured`, `interests` and `services`. `background.interests` is bucketed into `top_voices`, `companies`, `groups`, `schools` and `newsletters`, the same five tabs the `/v1/linkedin/profile/interests/*` endpoints sell separately. `similar_profiles` is LinkedIn's People-also-viewed rail, up to 20 members, which `/v1/linkedin/profile/similar` sells separately. `background.experiences[]` carries the skills tagged on each role, and `background.skills[]` carries `endorsements` plus `endorsement_notes`, none of which `/profile/complete` returns. THREE THINGS TO READ CAREFULLY. `section_totals` gives LinkedIn's own count for each section and it can EXCEED the array beside it, because long sections are truncated at source; trust `section_totals` for a count, never `background.<section>.length`. `author.ext.followers_approximate` is true when this source reported a rounded follower count instead of an exact one, which it does on large accounts; `/v1/linkedin/profile` returns the exact integer. `background.skills[].endorsements_is_floor` is true when LinkedIn published a \"99+\" style label instead of a number, so the count is a minimum. `background.services` is returned on this endpoint only, is passed through in the source's own shape, and is null for a member who publishes no services page, which is most members. `background.given_recommendations` is NOT returned: this source carries only what the member received, and an empty array would read as \"none given\"; use `/v1/linkedin/profile/complete` for those. Every top-level key of the original record is kept unchanged for compatibility.

**Use when** you want it for a one-call profile audit, in place of stacking profile, profile/complete, profile/stats, the five interests endpoints and profile/similar. **Not for** recent posts, which it does not return (linkedin/profile/with-posts, linkedin/profile/posts) or a company page (linkedin/profile/full).
**Cost** price moves with `urls` · cache 900 s
**Pricing** 5 credits for one profile with `url`. With `urls`, 5 credits per profile returned, from 5 for one profile up to 50 for the 10-profile maximum. Duplicate URLs are collapsed before the call and profiles that do not resolve are not charged, so a list with repeats or dead handles costs less than its length. A list where nothing resolves is a free 404.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (optional, string) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/`
- `urls` (optional, string) - Up to 10 full LinkedIn profile URLs in one call, comma separated. The response becomes `{items, total}` instead of a single profile. Billed 5 credits per profile RETURNED, the same rate as a single call: duplicates are collapsed before the call and profiles that do not resolve are not charged, so a list with repeats or dead handles costs less than its length. A list where nothing resolves is a free 404. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates,https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeffweiner08`

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `url`, `urls`.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {id string, publicIdentifier string, linkedinUrl string, firstName string, lastName string, emails array, headline string, websites string[], openToWork boolean, hiring boolean, premium boolean, influencer boolean, memorialized boolean, creator boolean, objectUrn string, registeredAt string}; `location` {linkedinText string, countryCode string}; `location.parsed` {text string, countryCode string, regionCode null, country string, countryFull string, state string, city string} (+262 more).

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.next_cursor`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/all" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/articles - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns the member's LinkedIn Pulse articles as a canonical PostList: `post.id`, `content.text`, `author`, engagement counts, and `published_at`. Pass the same profile URL `/v1/linkedin/profile` takes. Page with `page`.

**Use when** you want it for long-form writing. profile/posts is the short-form feed; article fetches one Pulse URL.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Paging** page (native `page`) · ≈19/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/19) x 5 credits · typical 1.4-1.5 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile whose articles to list. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - 1-based page number. Defaults to 1.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+17 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name, verified}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, saves, shares, views}; `post.ext` {reaction_counts}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null} (+1 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

**Next** `linkedin/article/comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - List comments on a LinkedIn Pulse article. · `linkedin/post/with-comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get a LinkedIn post together with its comments. · `linkedin/post/comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get LinkedIn post comments. · `linkedin/article` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get a LinkedIn Pulse article.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/articles" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/certifications - 5 credits (advanced)

List a member's licenses and certifications, normalised to the SocialCrawl schema. Each certification also carries its `credential_id`, when it expires (`expires_at`, as LinkedIn writes it, such as `Feb 2029`) and the issuer's LinkedIn page and logo (`authority_url`, `authority_logo`); each is null when the member gave none or the source that answered does not give it.

**Use when** you want to check formal credentials, as opposed to self-listed skills in profile/skills or degrees in profile/educations.

**Paging** page (native `page`) · page size not measured · depth unknown · typical 2.0-6.7 s

**Query params**

- `urn` (optional, string) - The member's opaque LinkedIn URN, as returned in `author.ext.urn` by /v1/linkedin/profile. Optional, and a pure optimisation: pass it ALONGSIDE `url` (which stays required) and this call skips the internal handle lookup, so it answers faster and consumes half the upstream rate-limit budget. ## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/comments - 5 credits (advanced)

Lists the comments a LinkedIn member has left on posts, newest first, as one fixed window of up to 20: each with the comment text, its time and reactions, and the post it was left on (text, media, author and engagement). When the primary source is momentarily rate-limited, a second source answers with the same comments in the same order, with the same text, dates and counts, but each image, logo and avatar list carries one size (the largest), a video's `duration`, `aspect_ratio`, stream sizes and thumbnail dimensions are null, the post author's `first_name` and `last_name` are null, and on a post with a ugcPost id (of any media type) `post.created_at` can be up to about two minutes later; `data._warnings` says so. From either source, `post.created_at` is the time the post was published, read from the post's id. From the second source each comment also carries its own link (`url`) and whether it was a contribution to a collaborative article (`is_contribution`), and its post carries the post it quotes (`post.reshared_post`) and the author's profile button (`post.author.website`, `post.author.website_label`); from the primary source these keys are null. A company author's `post.author.public_identifier` is its page handle.

**Use when** you want to track someone's activity in other conversations; post/comments returns the comments on one specific post.
**Cost** cache 300 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** single page - The upstream serves this feed as one fixed window: it ignores both `page` and its own continuation token and re-serves the first page forever (re-verified against the provider 04/09/2026), so there is no second page to fetch.

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile, company, or post. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/`
- `urn` (optional, string) - The member's opaque LinkedIn URN, as returned in `author.ext.urn` by /v1/linkedin/profile. Optional, and a pure optimisation: pass it ALONGSIDE `url` (which stays required) and this call skips the internal handle lookup, so it answers faster and consumes half the upstream rate-limit budget. Verified on the deployed API 05/09/2026. To address a member by URN alone, send the URN-form profile URL as `url`, for example https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAA8BYqEBCGLg_vT_ca6mMEqkpp9nVffJ3hc: it resolves to the same member as the public address (verified 20/10/2026 on profile/posts and profile/comments) and holds only ASCII, which helps when the public address carries an emoji or other symbol.

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]` (inferred from a sample): {urn string, comment string, created_at string}; `activity` {num_likes number, num_comments number, num_shares null}; `activity.reaction_counts[]` {count number, type string}; `post` {id string, post_type string, text string}; `post.content` {images null, document null}; `post.content.video.thumbnail[]` {width number, height number, url string, expires_at number}; `post.content.video` {duration string, aspect_ratio string}; `post.content.video.streams[]` {url string, expires_at number, size number, width number, height number, bit_rate number} (+26 more).

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/comments" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/complete - 10 credits (premium)

Returns a LinkedIn member's full background in one premium call, in place of `/v1/linkedin/profile` plus `/v1/linkedin/profile/experiences`, `/profile/educations`, `/profile/skills` and `/profile/recommendations`. Two keys carry it in SocialCrawl's own shapes. `author` is the same Author object `/v1/linkedin/profile` returns (`username`, `display_name`, `bio`, `location`, `avatar_url` and the `ext` flags, `urn` and `member_id` included); `followers` and `following` are null because this call reports no counts. `background` holds `summary` (the About text, or null) and five arrays whose items match the matching `/v1/linkedin/profile/*` endpoint item for item: `experiences` (`title`, `description`, `location`, `date` such as `{start: "Apr 2025", end: "Present"}`, `employment_type`, `skills`, `company` with `id`, `name`, `url` and `logo`), `educations` (`id`, `school`, `date`, `degree`), `skills` (`skill`, `is_passed_skill_assessment`), `recommendations` (received) and `given_recommendations` (`text`, `date`, `type`, `recommender`). A leaf this call does not carry is null rather than missing, for example a role's `skills` and a recommender's `urn`, and `educations` is an empty array when the member lists none. Every other top-level key (`firstName`, `fullPositions`, `languages`, `projects` and the rest) is the original packed record, kept unchanged for compatibility; languages and projects are only available there.

**Use when** you want it for background checks and enrichment, where one premium call replaces profile, profile/experiences, profile/educations, profile/skills and profile/recommendations. **Not for** follower or connection counts, which come back null (linkedin/profile/with-posts, linkedin/profile/all), or for recent posts (linkedin/profile/with-posts).
**Cost** cache 900 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/ryanroslansky/`

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {id number, urn string, username string, firstName string, lastName string, isTopVoice boolean, isCreator boolean, isPremium boolean, profilePicture string, summary string, headline string}; `profilePictures[]` {url string, width number, height number}; `backgroundImage[]` {width number, height number, url string}; `geo` {country string, city string, full string, countryCode string}; `languages[]` {name string, proficiency string}; `position[]` {companyId number, companyName string} (+137 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/complete" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/ryanroslansky/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/full - 5 credits (custom)

Fans out to the LinkedIn company profile and recent-posts endpoints in parallel and returns the unified author, the recent-post list, and computed metrics: avg_engagement_rate, avg_engagement_rate_by_followers, posting cadence (with the window it was measured over), the top post, and the format mix. avg_engagement_rate is view-based: the mean of each post's (likes + comments + shares) / views, so only posts that carry a view count contribute, and it is null when none does. avg_engagement_rate_by_followers is the mean of likes + comments per post divided by the account's follower count, over every post that carries both, so it covers posts with no view count. One call reads one page of recent posts, which on LinkedIn company is 10 posts, and computes the metrics over that page: `posts` can shorten the window but not lengthen it past one page, and `_warnings` says so when fewer posts came back than `posts` asked for. Pass `posts_cursor` back as `cursor` to read the next page, 5 credits a call. The profile leg is the only critical leg: if posts can't be fetched the call still returns the profile with post-dependent metrics null, and every leg's status is surfaced in legs[]. Flat 5 credits. This is a company-page composite: pass a `linkedin.com/company/{slug}` URL. Person `/in/` URLs belong on `/v1/linkedin/profile`. Posts are loaded from `/v1/linkedin/company/posts` using the numeric `company_id` the profile leg returns as `author.id`.

**Use when** you want it for a one-call company snapshot instead of calling company and company/posts and doing the engagement maths yourself. **Not for** a member's profile, because it takes company pages only (linkedin/profile/all for the whole profile, linkedin/profile/with-posts for counts and recent posts).
**Cost** cache 900 s
**Paging** cursor · page size not measured · depth unknown · typical 11-27 s

**Query params**

- `url` (optional, string) - Full LinkedIn company profile or page URL. One of the identity params is required. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/company/microsoft`
- `posts` (optional, integer) - How many of the fetched recent posts to return and compute the metrics over (1-100, default 25). One call reads one page, which on LinkedIn company is 10 posts, so a larger value returns that page and a `_warnings` note; pass posts_cursor back as cursor for the next page. · e.g. `25`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Pass a prior response's posts_cursor to read the next page of posts. Each call is a separate 5-credit call whose metrics cover that page only.
- `include` (optional, string) - CSV subset of posts,computed (default both). include=computed omits the raw posts[] array from the response to save payload. The metrics are computed from the same fetched posts either way, so they do not change.

**Constraints**

- `url` is required (it is optional in shape only - the request needs it).

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): `profile` {id string, username string, display_name string, avatar_url string, bio string, verified boolean, followers number, following null, posts_count null, likes_count null, url string, location string, private null, joined_at null}; `profile.ext` {website string, cover_url string, page_active boolean, employee_count number, founded_year null, specialities string[], industries string[]}; `profile.ext.employee_count_range` {start number, end null}; `profile.ext.headquarters` {country string, city string} (+65 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/full" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/company/microsoft" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)
