## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/images - 5 credits (advanced)

Lists the image posts on a LinkedIn member's profile, normalised to the same Post shape as every other SocialCrawl post endpoint: `post.id`, `post.url`, `post.content.media_urls` (the highest-resolution image LinkedIn publishes), `post.author` and `post.published_at`. LinkedIn does not expose the caption on this surface, so `content.text` is null; fetch the post by URL for the full record. `published_at` is the exact posting time, decoded from the post's id, and `post.ext.published_at_precision` is absent; on a row whose id cannot be decoded it falls back to LinkedIn's own relative label and the precision names the unit (hour, day, week or month).

**Use when** you only want photo posts; profile/posts returns every format and profile/videos returns the videos.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Paging** single page - The upstream serves this feed as one fixed window: it ignores both `page` and its own continuation token and re-serves the first page forever (re-verified against the provider 04/09/2026), so there is no second page to fetch.

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile, company, or post. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/`
- `urn` (optional, string) - The member's opaque LinkedIn URN, as returned in `author.ext.urn` by /v1/linkedin/profile. Optional, and a pure optimisation: pass it ALONGSIDE `url` (which stays required) and this call skips the internal handle lookup, so it answers faster and consumes half the upstream rate-limit budget. Verified on the deployed API 05/09/2026. To address a member by URN alone, send the URN-form profile URL as `url`, for example https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAA8BYqEBCGLg_vT_ca6mMEqkpp9nVffJ3hc: it resolves to the same member as the public address (verified 20/10/2026 on profile/posts and profile/comments) and holds only ASCII, which helps when the public address carries an emoji or other symbol.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

+13 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name}; `post.content` {media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, shares}; `post.ext` {published_at_precision, reaction_counts}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null, pinned null}; `post.ext` {author_url string}. Never filled: `post.author.verified`, `post.content.duration_seconds`, `post.content.text`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.views`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

**Next** `linkedin/post/with-comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get a LinkedIn post together with its comments. · `linkedin/post/comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get LinkedIn post comments. · `linkedin/post` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get LinkedIn post details.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/images" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/posts - 5-200 credits (request-shaped)

List a LinkedIn member's recent posts, normalised to the SocialCrawl schema. The upstream serves this feed as ONE fixed window and has no working continuation token, so the response is always terminal (`pagination.has_more` is `false` and `next_cursor` is `null`) and a `cursor` is rejected rather than silently re-serving the first page. Use `limit` to control depth: it defaults to 20 and accepts up to 100, the provider's hard ceiling. Up to 50 the call is a flat 5 credits; above 50 it is metered at 2 credits per post returned (see the credit cost). A feed shorter than the requested `limit` simply returns everything the member has posted. Posts the member reposted without comment are included, each as the original post, with the repost's own link in `post.url`. Where LinkedIn shows them, each post also carries the accounts it mentions and its linked text ranges (`post.ext.mentioned_accounts`, `post.ext.text_entities`, `post.ext.outbound_links`), whether it was edited or has comments turned off (`post.ext.is_edited`, `post.ext.comments_disabled`), its kind (`post.ext.type`, `post.ext.media_type`), a document, poll, job, event, celebration card or newsletter edition (`post.ext.document`, `post.ext.poll`, `post.ext.job`, `post.ext.event`, `post.ext.celebration`, `post.ext.newsletter`), the post it quotes (`post.ext.quoted_post`), who reposted it and when (`post.ext.reposted_by`, `post.ext.reposted_at`), the button on the author's profile (`post.ext.author_website`, `post.ext.author_website_label`) and a video's aspect ratio (`post.ext.aspect_ratio`); each is null when the post has none or it could not be read for that post.

**When the main source cannot answer**, a backup source serves the same window. Its rows carry the same fields, a document post's PDF in `content.media_urls` and its cover image in `content.thumbnail_url` included. Two fields can be missing on its rows, and `data._warnings` says so when they are: the preview image of a link share (`content.thumbnail_url`) and `post.ext.share_urn` on a repost.

**Older than the most recent 100.** Read the row count first: if this endpoint returns fewer posts than your `limit`, that is the member's entire history and there is nothing further back to fetch. If it returns exactly 100 the feed is truncated, and the way past it is /v1/linkedin/search/posts with `from_member` set to the member's urn (`author.ext.urn` on /v1/linkedin/profile) and no `query`. That endpoint pages with a real `next_cursor` that keeps advancing, and on a prolific member it reaches months further back than this one. It reads a best-effort search index rather than the member's feed, so it is the deeper source only for members this endpoint truncates. **It is not a complete archive**: how deep it goes is a property of the index and varies by member, from a couple of hundred posts to a few hundred, so walk it to find out and do not design around a fixed number.

**Use when** you want it for what a person posted themselves; profile/reactions covers posts they only reacted to, profile/comments their comments. **Not for** the profile and its counts (linkedin/profile/with-posts), a member's complete post history (linkedin/profile/posts/archive) or a company's posts (linkedin/company/posts).
**Cost** price moves with `limit` · cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits for a call with no `limit`, or `limit` at 50 or below. Above 50 the call is metered at 2 credits per post RETURNED: it holds `limit x 2` up front (the 100 maximum holds 200) and refunds down to the posts that actually came back, never below 5, so a member with 60 posts settles at 120 credits however high `limit` was set.
**Paging** single page - The upstream serves this feed as one fixed window with no working continuation token (re-verified against the provider 04/09/2026); use `limit` (up to 100, the provider's hard ceiling) to control how much of it you get in the one call.

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile, company, or post. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/`
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-100) - How many posts to return in the one call, 1 to 100. Defaults to the upstream's 20. 100 is the provider's hard ceiling. Up to 50 the call is a flat 5 credits; above 50 it is metered at 2 credits per post returned (holds `limit x 2`, never below 5). Ask for the depth you need up front - there is no second page to fetch.
- `urn` (optional, string) - The member's opaque LinkedIn URN, as returned in `author.ext.urn` by /v1/linkedin/profile. Optional, and a pure optimisation: pass it ALONGSIDE `url` (which stays required) and this call skips the internal handle lookup, so it answers faster and consumes half the upstream rate-limit budget. Verified on the deployed API 05/09/2026. To address a member by URN alone, send the URN-form profile URL as `url`, for example https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAA8BYqEBCGLg_vT_ca6mMEqkpp9nVffJ3hc: it resolves to the same member as the public address (verified 20/10/2026 on profile/posts and profile/comments) and holds only ASCII, which helps when the public address carries an emoji or other symbol.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

+34 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {display_name}; `post.content` {media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, shares}; `post.ext` {aspect_ratio, author_followers, author_website, author_website_label, celebration, comments_disabled, document, event, is_edited, is_repost_quote} (+15 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/posts" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/posts/archive - 5-500 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a LinkedIn member's posts read from their own feed rather than from a public search index, and it is **the only route that reaches a member's complete history**. Measured on one prolific member 07/09/2026: this endpoint walked about 1,800 posts back to June 2017 and then stopped because there was nothing older, while /v1/linkedin/profile/posts caps at 100 and walking /v1/linkedin/search/posts with `from_member` exhausts at about 395. How far back it reaches is a property of the member, not of this endpoint: when a page comes back with no `next_cursor`, you have everything. Each post carries the text, media, the exact publish timestamp, the full engagement breakdown including share counts and the reaction breakdown by type (`post.ext.reaction_counts`), and the author's photo, ids and headline (`post.author.avatar_url`, `post.ext.author_id`, `post.ext.author_urn`, `post.ext.author_headline`). Where LinkedIn shows them, each post also carries the accounts it mentions and its linked text ranges (`post.ext.mentioned_accounts`, `post.ext.text_entities`, `post.ext.outbound_links`), whether it was edited or has comments turned off (`post.ext.is_edited`, `post.ext.comments_disabled`), its kind (`post.ext.type`, `post.ext.media_type`), a document, poll, job, event, celebration card or newsletter edition (`post.ext.document`, `post.ext.poll`, `post.ext.job`, `post.ext.event`, `post.ext.celebration`, `post.ext.newsletter`), the post it quotes (`post.ext.quoted_post`), who reposted it and when (`post.ext.reposted_by`, `post.ext.reposted_at`), the button on the author's profile (`post.ext.author_website`, `post.ext.author_website_label`) and a video's aspect ratio (`post.ext.aspect_ratio`); each is null when the post has none or it could not be read for that post. **It is not the cheapest endpoint.** /v1/linkedin/profile/posts returns up to 50 posts for a flat 5 credits, or up to 100 at 2 credits a post, and is the whole history for most members, so start there and come here when it is not enough, or when you need what it cannot give you: an exact publish timestamp on every row instead of an approximation that shifts between calls, the share count, and a guarantee that every row was written by the member rather than reshared by them. **To walk the archive, pass `limit=100` and follow `next_cursor` until it stops coming back.** Follow it promptly: a `next_cursor` can expire about an hour after it was issued, and replaying an expired one answers a free 400 that says to start again from the first page. A `limit` below 100 returns that many of the newest posts and no cursor, because a partial page cannot be continued without silently skipping the rest of it. **Pricing is metered at 5 credits per post RETURNED**, so a member who has posted fewer than your `limit` costs less than you asked for, and a member with no posts costs nothing. Reposts are excluded, so every row you are charged for is one the member wrote. A profile we cannot find comes back as an empty list and costs nothing.

**Use when** Use it only when profile/posts (up to 100 posts; 5 credits to 50, then 2 per post) and search/posts with from_member run out of depth. Metered at 5 credits per post returned.
**Cost** price moves with `limit` · cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits per post RETURNED. The call holds `limit x 5` up front - the default limit of 20 holds 100 and the 100 maximum holds 500 - and refunds down to the posts that actually came back, so a member with 12 posts settles at 60 credits however high `limit` was set. This is the most expensive read on the platform per row: check whether /v1/linkedin/profile/posts (5 credits up to 50 posts, 2 a post above that) already covers the window you need before walking the archive With `max_pages`, `max_items` or `max_credits`, each page walked is billed at this price (a cached page is free), and `max_credits` caps the total.
**Paging** cursor (native `pagination_token`) · default page size not measured; set with `limit` · depth unknown · typical 4.0-5.5 s

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - The member's LinkedIn profile URL, for example https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/`
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-100) - How many posts to return, 1 to 100 (default 20). Pass 100 to walk the full archive: only a full page returns a `next_cursor`. You are charged 5 credits for each post actually returned, not for the limit you asked for. · e.g. `100`
- `pagination_token` (optional, string) - The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Omit it for the newest posts. A cursor can expire about an hour after it was issued; an expired one answers a free 400, and the walk restarts from the first page.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+38 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {display_name}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, shares}; `post.ext` {article, aspect_ratio, author_followers, author_headline, author_id, author_type, author_url, author_urn, author_website, author_website_label, celebration} (+19 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

**Next** `linkedin/post/with-comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get a LinkedIn post together with its comments. · `linkedin/post/comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get LinkedIn post comments. · `linkedin/post` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get LinkedIn post details.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/profile/posts/archive" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/recommendations - 5 credits (advanced)

Lists the recommendations a LinkedIn member received, or with `type=given` the ones they wrote, 20 per page, each with `text`, `date`, `type` (how the two members know each other, as LinkedIn words it, such as "Sam worked with Alex but they were at different companies") and `recommender` (on a given recommendation, `recommender` is the member who received it). When the primary source is momentarily rate-limited, a backup source answers the first page of received recommendations with the same recommendations in the same order, but `type` and the recommender's `urn`, `first_name`, `last_name` and `is_premium` are null. A later page, `type=given`, or a first page that backup cannot answer, comes from a second backup with the same recommendations and the same nulls, which also leaves out the recommender's `avatar`; `data._warnings` says so. Each recommendation also carries when it was last edited (`updated_at`, ISO 8601, null when the source that answered does not give it) and, with `type=given`, the member who received it (`recipient`, the same person as `recommender`); `recipient` is null on a received recommendation.

**Use when** you want it for written references, and set type to received or given to choose which side of the relationship you want.

- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - 1-based page number. Defaults to 1.
- `type` (optional, enum: received | given) - Filter by kind. See the allowed values.
- `urn` (optional, string) - The member's opaque LinkedIn URN, as returned in `author.ext.urn` by /v1/linkedin/profile. Optional, and a pure optimisation: pass it ALONGSIDE `url` (which stays required) and this call skips the internal handle lookup, so it answers faster and consumes half the upstream rate-limit budget. Verified on the deployed API 05/09/2026. To address a member by URN alone, send the URN-form profile URL as `url`, for example https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAA8BYqEBCGLg_vT_ca6mMEqkpp9nVffJ3hc: it resolves to the same member as the public address (verified 20/10/2026 on profile/posts and profile/comments) and holds only ASCII, which helps when the public address carries an emoji or other symbol.

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/videos - 5 credits (advanced)

Lists the video posts on a LinkedIn member's profile, normalised to the same Post shape as every other SocialCrawl post endpoint: `post.id`, `post.url`, `post.content.thumbnail_url`, `post.content.duration_seconds`, the reaction and comment counts on `post.engagement`, and the per-reaction-type breakdown on `post.ext.reaction_counts`. LinkedIn does not expose the caption on this surface, so `content.text` is null; fetch the post by URL for the full record. `published_at` is the exact posting time, decoded from the post's id, and `post.ext.published_at_precision` is absent; on a row whose id cannot be decoded it falls back to LinkedIn's own relative label and the precision names the unit (hour, day, week or month).

**Use when** you want to collect a person's videos, then pass a video post's URL to post/transcript to read what was said.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Paging** single page - The upstream serves this feed as one fixed window: it ignores both `page` and its own continuation token and re-serves the first page forever (re-verified against the provider 04/09/2026), so there is no second page to fetch.

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile, company, or post. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates/`
- `urn` (optional, string) - The member's opaque LinkedIn URN, as returned in `author.ext.urn` by /v1/linkedin/profile. Optional, and a pure optimisation: pass it ALONGSIDE `url` (which stays required) and this call skips the internal handle lookup, so it answers faster and consumes half the upstream rate-limit budget. Verified on the deployed API 05/09/2026. To address a member by URN alone, send the URN-form profile URL as `url`, for example https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAA8BYqEBCGLg_vT_ca6mMEqkpp9nVffJ3hc: it resolves to the same member as the public address (verified 20/10/2026 on profile/posts and profile/comments) and holds only ASCII, which helps when the public address carries an emoji or other symbol.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

+13 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes, shares}; `post.ext` {published_at_precision, reaction_counts}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null, pinned null}; `post.ext` {author_url string}. Never filled: `post.author.verified`, `post.content.media_urls`, `post.content.text`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.views`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

**Next** `linkedin/post/with-comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get a LinkedIn post together with its comments. · `linkedin/post/comments` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get LinkedIn post comments. · `linkedin/post/reposts` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - List reposts of a LinkedIn post. · `linkedin/post/reactions` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - List reactors on a LinkedIn post.

## GET /v1/linkedin/profile/with-posts - 10 credits (premium)

Returns a LinkedIn member's profile, follower and connection counts, and recent posts in one premium call. `author` is the same Author object `/v1/linkedin/profile` returns, with `followers` and `following` filled from this call's counts. `posts` is an array of recent posts whose items match `/v1/linkedin/profile/posts` item for item (`post.id` is the activity id, `post.published_at` is the exact posting time, `post.ext.reaction_counts` breaks reactions down by type), so `post.ext.published_at_precision` is null: there is no approximation to declare. `background` holds `summary` (the About text, or null) and `experiences`, `educations` and `skills` arrays whose items match the matching `/v1/linkedin/profile/*` endpoint item for item; a leaf this call does not carry is null rather than missing. This call carries no recommendations; use `/v1/linkedin/profile/complete` for those. Every other top-level key is the original profile record, kept unchanged for compatibility.

**Use when** you want it for one call covering the counts, recent posts and career history. Use profile/complete when you need recommendations. **Not for** recommendations or the full background (linkedin/profile/complete, linkedin/profile/all) or a company page (linkedin/profile/full).
**Cost** cache 900 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Full URL of the LinkedIn profile. · e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/adamselipsky/`

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {id number, urn string, username string, firstName string, lastName string, isTopVoice boolean, isCreator boolean, isPremium boolean, profilePicture string, summary string, headline string}; `profilePictures[]` {url string, width number, height number}; `backgroundImage[]` {width number, height number, url string}; `geo` {country string, city string, full string, countryCode string}; `educations[].start` {year number, month number, day number}; `educations[].end` {year number} (+149 more).

```bash

  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/adamselipsky/" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/search/companies - 10 credits (premium)

Returns company pages matching a keyword, as a canonical AuthorList: `username`, `display_name`, `bio` (tagline), `url`, `avatar_url`, and `author.ext.company_id` (the numeric id the other `/company/*` endpoints take). Optional filters: `company_size` (LinkedIn headcount buckets), `has_jobs`, `industry_ids` (comma-separated ids from `/v1/linkedin/search/industry`), `geocode` (ids from `/v1/linkedin/search/location`). Page with `page`. When the main source is unavailable, the first page is answered by a second source with the same fields; a later page or `has_jobs=true` has no second source and returns an error to retry. A search with no matches is free, and that empty answer is cached for 6 hours; send `Cache-Control: no-cache` to search again sooner.

**Use when** you want to find companies by name and optional size, industry, location, or open-jobs filters, then pass a result to company.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** page (native `page`) · ≈10/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/10) x 10 credits · typical 2.9-9.1 s

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Company name or keyword. · e.g. `microsoft`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - 1-based page number. Defaults to 1.
- `company_size` (optional, enum: 1-10 | 11-50 | 51-200 | 201-500 | 501-1000 | 1001-5000 | 5001-10000 | 10001+) - Headcount bucket. One of `1-10`, `11-50`, `51-200`, `201-500`, `501-1000`, `1001-5000`, `5001-10000`, `10001+`.
- `has_jobs` (optional, boolean) - When true, return only companies that currently have open jobs.
- `industry_ids` (optional, string) - Comma-separated industry ids from /v1/linkedin/search/industry.
- `geocode` (optional, string) - Comma-separated location ids from /v1/linkedin/search/location.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

|---|---|

| `author.ext.company_id` | Numeric company id, which is what the LinkedIn company… |
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description |

+8 more (types in the full schema): `author` {display_name, followers, following, likes_count, posts_count, verified}; `author.ext` {business_hours, products}. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

## GET /v1/linkedin/search/people - 10-50 credits (request-shaped)

Searches LinkedIn members by name and B2B filters (title, current/past company, school, industry, location, language). Returns a paginated list of matching profiles with handle, headline, location, follower count, and the member URN for follow-up enrichment calls. Each page is 10 members. On a plain call `author.followers` is LinkedIn's rounded display bucket, and only on the rows that show one (flagged `author.ext.followers_approximate: true`), and `author.following` is null on every row. Send `include=profile` and every row is joined, in the same call, to the member's profile lookup (`/v1/linkedin/profile`): `author.followers` becomes the exact follower count and `author.ext.followers_approximate` reads false on every row the lookup filled, whether the row arrived with LinkedIn's rounded bucket or with no count at all, `author.following` is filled with the member's connection count (on LinkedIn a member's `following` is the number of connections), and the location, the joined date (`author.joined_at`), and the country, website, cover image and profile flags on `author.ext` land where the row lacks them. Cost: 10 credits for the list; include=profile holds 4 credits per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup, so a call costs at most 50; rows already in cache are free and unfilled rows are refunded. Pass `limit` (1 to 10) to join only the top rows: `limit=3&include=profile` costs at most 22. Time: the lookups run in parallel, about 1 second for 10 rows, up to 3 on a slow second, and never more than 8 seconds. The response carries a `hydration` block itemising rows, lookups, cache hits, credits and milliseconds.

**Use when** you want to build a prospect list by job title, company, school, or location; use company/people to list one employer's staff.
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 10 credits for the list. include=profile holds 4 credits per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup: at most 50 for the 10-row page, or 10 + 4 x limit when you pass `limit`. Rows served from cache are free, unfilled rows are refunded, and a repeat of a fully joined page within the list's cache window costs 0. The list is cached for 2 minutes and each profile lookup for 15 minutes. With `max_pages`, `max_items` or `max_credits`, each page walked is billed at this price (a cached page is free), and `max_credits` caps the total.
**Paging** page (native `page`) · default page size not measured; set with `limit` · depth unknown · typical 8.6-27 s

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Name or display-name keyword to search for (e.g. 'Bill Gates'). · e.g. `Bill Gates`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - Page number for pagination (default 1).
- `first_name` (optional, string) - Filter by first name.
- `last_name` (optional, string) - Filter by last name.
- `title` (optional, string) - Filter by job title or headline.
- `current_company` (optional, string) - Filter by current company, using a numeric company id from /v1/linkedin/company (`author.id`). Comma-separated for multiple. · e.g. `1035`
- `past_company` (optional, string) - Filter by a previously-worked company, using a numeric company id from /v1/linkedin/company (`author.id`). · e.g. `1035`
- `school` (optional, string) - Filter by school, using a school id from /v1/linkedin/search/schools (`id`). · e.g. `1792`
- `industry` (optional, string) - Filter by industry, using an industry id from /v1/linkedin/search/industry (`industry_id`). · e.g. `4`
- `geocode_location` (optional, string) - Filter by location, using a geocode id from /v1/linkedin/search/location (`geocode`). · e.g. `103644278`
- `profile_language` (optional, string) - Filter by profile language (ISO 2-letter code, e.g. 'en').
- `service_category` (optional, string) - Filter by service category, using a numeric service-category id. No endpoint resolves these, so pass one you already hold. · e.g. `1`
- `follower_of` (optional, string) - Return people who follow a specific member, using the member's URN from /v1/linkedin/profile (`author.ext.urn`). This one is a URN and not a numeric id. · e.g. `ACoAAA8BYqEBCGLg_vT_ca6mMEqkpp9nVffJ3hc`
- `include` (optional, enum: profile) - Set to `profile` (one token only) to join every row to the member's profile lookup in this one call: `author.followers` becomes the exact count and `author.ext.followers_approximate` reads false on every row the lookup filled, `author.following` is filled with the member's connection count, and the location, joined date, country, website, cover image and profile flags land where the row lacks them. Holds 4 credits per row and keeps only the rows filled from a fresh lookup; rows already in cache and rows that could not be filled are refunded, so a call costs at most 50 (10 + 4 per row) and the usual bill is lower. Adds about 1 second for 10 rows, up to 3 on a slow second and never more than 8, and nothing when the members are already cached; read `data.hydration` for the rows, the credits held and kept, and the time.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-10) - Take the top N rows of this page (1 to 10). With `include=profile` it caps both the rows joined and the extra credits: `limit=3&include=profile` costs at most 22. The page cursor still advances past the full page of 10, so the rows past your limit are skipped, not carried to the next page. Without `include=profile` the call stays 10 credits.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |

+22 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, following, joined_at, likes_count, location, posts_count, verified}; `author.ext` {business_hours, country, cover_url, followers_approximate, is_creator, is_hiring, is_influencer, is_open_to_work, is_premium, is_top_voice, joined_at_precision, member_id} (+3 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.hydration`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/linkedin/search/people" \
  --data-urlencode "query=Bill Gates" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/linkedin/search/posts - 1-56 credits (request-shaped)

Finds public LinkedIn posts, feed updates, and Pulse articles. Most answers carry the full post text, the author with their avatar, every image, video and document attached to the post, the video length, and the like, comment and share counts with the reaction breakdown. Every row carries the exact publish time, read from the post id rather than estimated. When the main source cannot answer a request, a backup source answers it, with shorter text and, on some backups, no media. Where LinkedIn shows them, each post also carries its author's ids, kind, page follower count, Premium flag and profile button (`post.ext.author_id`, `post.ext.author_urn`, `post.ext.author_type`, `post.ext.author_followers`, `post.ext.author_is_premium`, `post.ext.author_website`, `post.ext.author_website_label`), its share urn (`post.ext.share_urn`), the accounts it mentions and its web links (`post.ext.mentioned_accounts`, `post.ext.outbound_links`), whether it was edited or has comments turned off (`post.ext.is_edited`, `post.ext.comments_disabled`), its kind (`post.ext.type`, `post.ext.media_type`), a link card, newsletter edition, document, poll, job, event, celebration card or group (`post.ext.article`, `post.ext.newsletter`, `post.ext.document`, `post.ext.poll`, `post.ext.job`, `post.ext.event`, `post.ext.celebration`, `post.ext.group`), the post it quotes (`post.ext.quoted_post`), a video's aspect ratio (`post.ext.aspect_ratio`) and an image's content credentials and AI label (`post.ext.content_credentials`, `post.ext.ai_label`); each is null when the post has none or the source that answered does not send it. Use `date_posted` to narrow to recent posts and follow `next_cursor` to walk deeper; `page` still works.

**Brand and people mentions.** Add `mentions_company` (numeric company ids) or `mentions_member` (member urns) to keep only posts that tag that company or person, for example `query=ai&mentions_company=1035` for posts about AI that mention Microsoft. Every row returned mentions one of them. They combine with `query`, `from_member` or `from_company`, page only by `next_cursor`, and answer 503 at no charge, never unfiltered posts, when they cannot be applied. A few combinations are refused with a 400 at no charge, each naming the fix: `content_type=collaborative_articles`, a `#hashtag` query with `sort_by=date_posted`, more than 5 `AND`, `OR` or `NOT` operators, and a `from_member` or `from_company` that is not a member urn or numeric company id. A narrow filter can return a short page, or older posts only, even with `sort_by=date_posted`; that is the real answer and is returned as it is. A first page with no matches is free, and that empty answer is cached for 1 hour; send `Cache-Control: no-cache` to search again sooner.

**Many posts in one call.** Pass `limit` (1 to 200) with a `query` and the call reads as many pages as it needs, removes duplicates, and returns up to that many posts in relevance order, charged 1 credit for every 5 posts returned, so 200 posts is 40 credits. Repeat the identical call inside the 2-minute cache window and it is served from cache for nothing. The response carries a `walk` summary saying how many pages were read and why the call stopped.

**Reading one member's back catalogue.** Pass `from_member` on its own, with no `query`, and page through the result: this is the only way to reach a member's posts older than the 100 that /v1/linkedin/profile/posts can return, and unlike that endpoint it hands you a real `next_cursor` that keeps advancing. Get the urn from `author.ext.urn` on /v1/linkedin/profile. Those results come back newest-first; `sort_by=relevance` is rejected on a subject-only call because there is no query for them to be relevant to.

**This is not a complete history, and how much it returns varies by member.** It reads a public search index, so it holds whatever that index holds for a given profile and no more. Measured 06/09/2026: one prolific member exhausted at 395 posts, while a customer walking his own profile of 800+ posts reached 223. Neither number is a limit you can raise by paging harder; the walk simply ends when the index runs out. Treat the depth as unknown until you walk it, and do not design around a fixed figure. For a member whose /v1/linkedin/profile/posts call already returns fewer posts than the `limit` you asked for, that feed is their whole history and this endpoint returns less, not more.

**Use when** you want it for broad keyword monitoring; it reads public search results, so treat coverage as best effort rather than complete.
**Cost** price moves with `label`, `limit` · cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits per page. Relevance against your query (by default, or with relevance=) is free. Adding relevant_to= holds 8 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 rows that were newly judged: rows already judged for the same topic are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free. The default labels (sponsored, intent, niche) are free. label=mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection, or label=intent with offer=, holds 8 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 posts that were newly judged: posts already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free. With `max_pages`, `max_items` or `max_credits`, each page walked is billed at this price (a cached page is free), and `max_credits` caps the total.
**Paging** page (native `page`) · default page size not measured; set with `limit` · depth unknown · typical 3.0-27 s

**Query params**

- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - 1-based page number. Defaults to 1. Following `next_cursor` is the better way to walk deeper.
- `sort_by` (optional, enum: date_posted | relevance) - Result ordering: `relevance` (default) or `date_posted`. On a subject-only call (`from_member` or `from_company` with no `query`) the results are ordered by date and `relevance` is rejected, because there is no query for them to be relevant to.
- `date_posted` (optional, enum: past_24h | past_week | past_month) - Date filter. One of `past_24h`, `past_week`, `past_month` (underscores, not hyphens). Note the JOB endpoints use `past_24_hours` for the same concept; the two vocabularies are not interchangeable. · e.g. `past_week`
- `content_type` (optional, enum: videos | photos | jobs | live_videos | documents | collaborative_articles) - Narrow to one kind of post.
- `from_company` (optional, string) - Filter to posts from a company, by numeric LinkedIn company id (for example `1035`). A company slug or URL is rejected; read the id from `author.id` on /v1/linkedin/company.
- `from_member` (optional, string) - Filter to posts from one member, by their LinkedIn member urn — the bare `ACoAA…` value published as `author.ext.urn` by /v1/linkedin/profile. A profile URL, a public slug (`williamhgates`) or a `urn:li:fsd_profile:`-prefixed value is rejected, because the source cannot use any of them. Pass this on its own, with no `query`, to walk one member's back catalogue.
- `query` (optional, string) - Keyword or phrase to search for. Optional when `from_member` or `from_company` is set: omit it to get that subject's posts unfiltered, and note that supplying a real content word narrows the results to posts matching it. · e.g. `ai agents`
- `mentions_member` (optional, string) - Only posts that mention these members (they are tagged in the post). Up to 10 LinkedIn member urns, comma separated: the bare `ACoAA…` value /v1/linkedin/profile publishes as `author.ext.urn`.
- `mentions_company` (optional, string) - Only posts that mention these company pages. Up to 10 numeric LinkedIn company ids, comma separated (for example `1035`), the id /v1/linkedin/company publishes as `author.id`.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-200) - Return up to this many posts in one call, 1 to 200. The call reads as many pages as it needs, removes duplicates, and is charged 1 credit for every 5 posts returned (200 posts = 40 credits). Repeating the identical call inside the 2-minute cache window is free. Requires `query`. Cannot be combined with `page` or `cursor`: the result always starts at the top and `pagination.next_cursor` is null. `pagination.has_more` says whether more posts were available when the call stopped, and `walk.stopped` says why it stopped (`limit`, `exhausted`, `deadline` or `sources_unavailable`).
- `ai_written_threshold` (optional, string) - Optional, only with label=ai_written and exclude=ai_written. The p (0 to 1) at which exclude=ai_written drops a post. Default 0.95 (level likely). 0.71 also drops possible posts: more AI posts go, and more posts by people with them.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `label` (sponsored | mention | intent | niche | quality | ai_style | ai_written | injection; paid: mention, quality, ai_style, ai_written, injection) · `exclude` (engagement_bait | ai_style | ai_written) · `label_evidence` (1) · `brand` · `brand_description` · `offer` · `relevance` (score | filter) · `relevant_to` · `relevance_threshold` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality); `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `query`, `from_member`, `from_company`.
- `ai_written_threshold` is a no-op without `label` - sending it alone is a free 400.
- `relevance_threshold`, `relevant_to` are no-ops without `relevance` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `exclude`, `brand`, `brand_description`, `offer`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `label`: at most 8 comma-separated values.
- `exclude`: at most 3 comma-separated values.

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+35 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, labels_evidence, language, relevance, save_rate}; `computed.labels` {ai_style, ai_written, injection, intent, mention, niche, quality, sponsored}; `post.author` {avatar_url, display_name}; `post.content` {media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments} (+16 more).
